nodes.title: Measurement-validity finding. Until 2026-10-21, the sim lab's runner.mjs never opened /api/studio/stream and never called GET /api/studio/slot, so the decided child's screen came only from the turn response's ui.studioSlot. A board that landed about 1 s after the reply (slot 'planning' with no artifact) was shown to the child as nothing drawn. Affected: 1,521 turns in 938 of 3,729 lessons with board pages, across 65 runs (agent-gate runs 21-57 such turns each, board-content and board-* runs 24-81, rel14x 36-card runs 18-24, voice-cont runs 11-52). The judges always saw the boards through boardPages, so judgements of the teacher's own board claims stand. Any judgement that rests on the CHILD saying 'screen pe kuch nahi / drawing nahi dikhaya' right after a planning slot is suspect, and so are follows_child and channel_truth scores driven by such complaints. Found while root-causing 38aad918 (subscribers:0 on every reveal, boards drawn at t5/t6). The runner now opens the stream and waits for the artifact (SIMLAB_WIRE, default on; SIMLAB_WIRE=off reproduces the old harness for A/B).

Tried and wrong since the sim lab began: a simulated child whose screen is only the turn response's ui.studioSlot. What broke: every board that landed after the reply (planning, then the artifact about 1 s later) was invisible to the child: 1,521 turns in 938 lessons across 65 runs. The child's 'nothing on screen' complaints that followed were harness artifacts, and they fed follows_child / channel_truth judgements. The fix: subscribe the way the real client does (fd-r5-simlab-harness-late-boards).

md.rejected:
## rj-r5-simlab-turn-only-screen — a simulated child that sees only the turn response (2026-10-21)

The sim lab's child saw only what the turn response carried. A board that arrived a second later never reached it. 1,521 turns in 938 lessons across 65 runs showed the child an empty screen that the real client would have filled. Judgements that rest on the child's 'nothing on screen' after a planning slot are not evidence of a product failure. A simulated client must subscribe to everything the real client subscribes to.
